# NestEgg — Full LLM Reference

> Comprehensive machine-readable reference to NestEgg, suitable for RAG
> ingestion, retrieval-augmented answers, and agent planning. Short
> version at /llms.txt.

## 1. Product overview

NestEgg is a privacy-first budget and expense tracker for individuals,
couples, and families. It runs entirely in the visitor's browser using
`localStorage` as the single source of truth. There is no backend, no
account, no telemetry, and no network dependency after the initial page
load. It is distributed as a free, MIT-licensed open-source project.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/dnzengou/budget-tracker
- **Live URL:**   https://nestegg.vercel.app/
- **Author:**     desiredsolutions.me
- **License:**    MIT
- **Current version:** 0.5.0 (see `package.json`)

## 2. Who is it for

- Individuals who want a simple, trustworthy expense tracker without
  signing up for a cloud service.
- Couples sharing finances but wanting to keep attribution per person.
- Families (2+ members) tracking spending across a shared budget.
- Developers interested in offline-first PWAs, SPA security hardening,
  and privacy-by-design.

## 3. Feature inventory

### 3.1 Onboarding
- Choose mode: `individual`, `couple`, or `family` (sets the number of
  prompt-for-name slots).
- Enter one name per household member.
- Pick a default display currency from a list of 14 ISO 4217 codes.
- "Start tracking" seeds the store and lands the user on the login screen.

### 3.2 Authentication
- Two roles: **Admin** (full read/write) and **Guest** (read-only view).
- Role is chosen by the password typed at login; the username field is a
  display label only and is not compared.
- Defaults: Admin = `admin123`, Guest = `guest`. Rotated by setting
  `VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` / `VITE_GUEST_PASSWORD` environment variables
  in the hosting platform (Vercel) before build.
- Passwords are inlined into the client bundle at build time and are
  therefore readable by anyone who inspects the JavaScript. Admins should
  not reuse a password from any other system.
- Rate limiting: five incorrect attempts in one tab trigger a 30-second
  in-memory cooldown. Both inputs and the login button are disabled during
  the cooldown with a live per-second countdown. State resets on reload.
- The `auth` slice of the store is deliberately NOT persisted to
  localStorage, so a devtools edit of `isAdmin` does not survive refresh.

### 3.3 Transactions
- Add, edit, and delete income and expense transactions.
- Mark recurring to flag monthly/weekly items in Insights.
- Auto-categorization: typed-aware keyword mapping (e.g. "salary" in an
  expense note does NOT get filed as income salary).
- Full-text search and type/category filters on the Transactions tab.
- CSV import and export (round-trip; same schema).

### 3.4 Budgets
- Per-category monthly caps.
- Dashboard surfaces budget pressure per category (% consumed).

### 3.5 Dashboard
- Four KPI tiles: income, spending, net, savings rate.
- 6-month trend bar chart.
- Category breakdown pie chart.
- All figures in the active currency, formatted via `Intl.NumberFormat`.

### 3.6 Insights
- Pure deterministic rule engine, no LLM calls.
- Rules: budget breach, month-over-month swing, top spending lever,
  savings-rate change, recurring-charge audit.

### 3.7 Admin utilities
- 🔑 Credentials dialog — shows both role username/password pairs with
  copy buttons and rotation instructions.
- ↺ Reset — wipes all browser-local data after confirmation.
- ↦ Logout — clears the auth slice.

## 4. Data model (summary)

Stored under `localStorage['nestegg-v1']` as JSON:

```ts
{
  settings: { mode, currency, onboarded },
  members:  Array<{ id, name }>,
  transactions: Array<{
    id, date, memberId, type: 'income'|'expense',
    category, note, amountCents, recurring
  }>,
  budgets: Array<{ categoryId, monthlyCents }>,
  // auth: intentionally NOT persisted
}
```

Local-time month keys (YYYY-MM) are used everywhere; UTC is avoided so
users west of UTC don't lose/gain a day on rollovers.

## 5. Technical stack

| Layer    | Choice                                              |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| UI       | React 19 + Vite 7 + TypeScript 5.9 (strict)         |
| Styling  | Tailwind 3.4 + shadcn/ui (Radix primitives, pruned to actual consumers) |
| Charts   | recharts                                            |
| State    | `useReducer` + Context, selective localStorage persist |
| Router   | react-router 7 (one `/` route)                      |
| Icons    | lucide-react                                        |
| Toasts   | sonner                                              |
| Build    | Vite with `manualChunks` split into charts / radix / router / icons / vendor |
| Deploy   | Vercel (auto-detect Vite preset)                    |
| CI       | GitHub Actions (lint + build), CodeQL, Dependabot   |

## 6. Security posture

- CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff,
  Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy — all declared in `vercel.json`.
- No remote network calls at runtime; CSP `connect-src 'self'`.
- Auth state excluded from persistence.
- Login rate limit (see §3.2).
- Secrets threat model: there are none. Passwords are UX gates, not
  cryptographic secrets.
- See `SECURITY.md` for the reporting policy.

## 7. Distribution

- Primary channel: Vercel auto-deploy from `main`.
- CI validation: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on every PR and push.
- Security scanning: `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` weekly + on PR.
- Dependency updates: `.github/dependabot.yml` grouped weekly.
- Vendored dev tooling under `tools/claude-skills-sdk/` and `tools/evoforge/`,
  excluded from Vercel builds via `.vercelignore`.

## 8. AI-crawler policy

All AI/LLM user agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot,
Applebot-Extended, Amazonbot, Bytespider, cohere-ai, Meta-ExternalAgent,
Meta-ExternalFetcher, DuckAssistBot, YouBot, MistralAI-User, OAI-SearchBot,
ChatGPT-User, Claude-Web, Claude-SearchBot, Perplexity-User) are explicitly
allowed to crawl all paths. No user data is served from this origin, so
there is nothing private to protect. See `/robots.txt`.

The site declares itself human-authored via
`<meta name="ai-content-declaration" content="human-authored">`.

Structured data (Schema.org `SoftwareApplication`) is embedded as JSON-LD
in `index.html`.

## 9. How to install

**As a web app:** visit the live URL. No signup.

**As a PWA:** in a Chromium-based browser, use the browser's "Install"
option from the address bar or menu. The app installs as a standalone
window, works offline after first load, and appears in the OS app launcher.

**From source:**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/dnzengou/budget-tracker.git
cd budget-tracker
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
npm run build    # dist/ → deploy anywhere static
```

## 10. Common tasks (for agent planning)

- "Add a transaction" → log in as admin → header **+ Add** button →
  fill type / amount / category / note → save.
- "Change currency" → Onboarding (first run) OR a planned Settings tab.
- "Export your data" → Transactions tab → Export CSV.
- "Import a bank statement" → Transactions tab → Import CSV (must match
  schema: date, type, category, note, amount, member).
- "Share read-only access" → log in as admin → 🔑 key icon → copy the
  Guest password → hand it to the viewer.
- "Rotate passwords" → set `VITE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` + `VITE_GUEST_PASSWORD`
  in Vercel → redeploy.
- "Wipe all data" → log in as admin → ↺ icon → confirm.

## 11. Explicitly out of scope

- Multi-device sync (would require a backend; conflicts with privacy
  posture).
- Bank API integration (Plaid etc. — would require a server).
- AI-generated insights (the engine is deterministic by design; LLM
  queries are left to the user, with `/llms-full.txt` providing the
  context they need).
- Multi-user cloud mode (the app is single-device by philosophy).

## 12. Changelog pointer

See `BLUEPRINT.md` for the full versioned changelog. Currently v0.5.0.
